thread:
lina: Heads-up — getting customer-reported P99 spikes on /v1/generate for acct `acme-inc`. Correlated with KV/prefix cache miss rate jump in us-west-2. ops alert fired at 1729456700.
eng-runtime-bot: ALERT: high_p99_latency{route="/v1/generate",region="us-west-2"} > 2s for 5m, flapping.
raj: grabbing traces. can you paste the prometheus query you saw?
support-ops: Query I used: `sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total[5m])) by (node) / sum(rate(kv_cache_request_total[5m])) by (node)` — miss rate from ~3% -> ~22% over the last hour for the cluster serving acme-inc.
sophie: also seeing a big rise in cache evictions: `kv_cache_evictions_total` spiked at the same time, looks like periodic thrash.
matt: any recent deploys to runtime or config changes to cache size/ttl?
carla: no code deploys in the last 12 hours, but we flipped a routing policy for burst capacity for enterprise customers at 05:12 UTC. Could that increase cardinality?
lina: timeline: 04:58 customer traffic increase -> 05:12 routing policy enabled -> 05:18 latency rise. Suggests cache warmup + churn.
raj: pulling a span. here's typical tail of slow request: ```
span_id=0xabc123 service=runtime model=gpt-rlhf seq_len=1024
kv_lookup: 120ms (hot) -> miss_count=1
kv_prefetch: started
wait_for_batch: 800ms
```
sophie: wait_for_batch 800ms — that's the main p99 contributor. If KV lookups miss, we rebuild prefix KV which is expensive and blocks batching.
matt: is the cache key normalization bug (old) still possible? I remember we had an issue where trailing whitespace in prompt prefixes created distinct keys.
carla: Good call — I found many unique keys for acme-inc: `prefix_len_40_hash_*` with high cardinality in the 1h window. Looks like clients send small prompt variations — adding user metadata into the prefix.
raj: repro steps: 1) run load test with many tiny prefix variants 2) watch `kv_cache_key_cardinality` and `kv_cache_evictions_total` 3) measure p95/p99. I can run a quick repro on staging.
lina: short mitigation we can try now: 1) increase KV cache max_entries on the deployment serving acme-inc from 200k -> 600k 2) temporarily switch eviction policy from pure LRU -> adaptive LFU to avoid thrash 3) enable prefix canonicalization (strip trailing whitespace + clamp user meta) behind FF.
sophie: for 2) is LFU available as a hot config toggle? we can toggle via runtime-config service.
matt: yes, runtime-config supports eviction_policy and max_entries. I'm pushing a config patch to canary.
eng-runtime-bot: deploy_bot: runtime-config patch rolled to canary (canary cluster id=can-7) at 1729456825.
carla: also adding a short-term routing policy: send acme-inc traffic to dedicated pool with larger cache while we stabilize. That routing change is live in canary and will be gradual.
raj: staging repro done: with chaotic prefix variants p99 jumped from 430ms -> 2.1s and kv_miss_rate from 4% -> 27%. After increasing max_entries and switching to LFU, p99 dropped to 460ms in staging.
lina: excellent. let's promote config to prod but do a canary rollout 10% for 10 minutes and watch p95/p99 and evictions. Rollback plan: revert runtime-config if p99 doesn't improve after 15m.
support-ops: I notified the support lead at acme-inc and opened a ticket with the recommended mitigations.
sophie: long-term: we should do two things — 1) add automatic prefix normalization in the prompt pipeline to reduce key cardinality, 2) add adaptive cache sizing per-customer based on unique key cardinality metric.
matt: opened GH issues for both proposals. Also adding more granular metrics: kv_cache_key_cardinality{customer}, kv_cache_evictions_rate{customer} so we can auto-detect thrash.
carla: action items: matt -> promote config to prod canary (10%), raj -> run slow-query traces during canary, sophie -> implement prefix normalization RFC, lina -> coordinate customer comms + postmortem.
lina: thanks everyone. keeping this thread as the live incident notes. Will update when prod canary hits 10% and after 15m window. :thumbsup:
eng-runtime-bot: METRICS: canary rollout at 1729456860 -> current kv_miss_rate in canary 6% (baseline 4%), p99 520ms.
lina: rolling to 10% now. last_message_ts=1729456905
